```python
import hashlib

def check_login(stored_hash: str, stored_salt: str, password: str) -> bool:
    salt = stored_salt[:16]  # first 16 bytes of salt
    hash_password = hashlib.pbkdf2_hmac('sha256', password, salt, 100000)  # hash the password with the salt
    return hash_password == stored_hash[16:]  # compare the last 16 bytes of the stored hash
```

Dependency confusion is a type of supply-chain attack that targets software packages by manipulating their dependencies. In this attack, an attacker replaces a legitimate package with a malicious one that has the same name and version number, but with malicious code. When the package is installed, it will execute the malicious code instead of the intended functionality. This can lead to unauthorized access, data theft, or other malicious activities. Dependency confusion can occur through various means, such as tampering with package manifests, injecting malicious code into package files, or exploiting vulnerabilities in package management systems. It is crucial to have robust security measures in place to prevent and detect dependency confusion attacks.
